188:t_1:4.en:
$$エイミー$$
「...Wow! There are so many $$ユンボロ$$!」

188:t_1:5.en:
$$ピニオン$$
「You don't get it, $$エイミー$$. The machines lined up in this $$ラー・カイラム$$ are called mobile suits.」

188:t_1:6.en:
$$アストナージ$$
「$$ピニオン$$! Stop talking and get to work! We're running out of time!」

188:t_1:8.en:
$$アストナージ$$
「Stop calling me Boss. Call me Chief.」

188:t_1:10.en:
$$アストナージ$$
「...Whatever... I give up. Just get to work.」

188:t_1:11.en:
$$ランド$$
「Let's get started, $$ピニオン$$. Our job is servicing the ballute packs, just in case we need them.」

188:t_1:12.en:
$$ピニオン$$
「You got it, $$ランド$$! I'll show you why they called me $$ガルガンティア$$'s best repairman!」

188:t_1:13.en:
$$メール$$
「Hey, $$アストナージ$$. How good is $$ピニオン$$, really?」

188:t_1:14.en:
$$アストナージ$$
「That 《$$残されの海$$》 he came from was apparently a very unusual environment. He certainly lacks experience.」

188:t_1:15.en:
$$アストナージ$$
「But he's got potential. With training, he should make a good mechanic.」

188:t_1:16.en:
$$エイミー$$
「Huh... So $$ピニオン$$'s working hard too.」

188:t_1:17.en:
$$チェーン$$
「$$ピニオン$$. When you're done there, please service the ASes too.」

188:t_1:18.en:
$$ピニオン$$
「You got it, sis! Leave it to me!」

188:t_1:19.en:
$$アストナージ$$
「As you can see, he adapts well too.」

188:t_1:20.en:
$$エイミー$$
「That's a relief. We've... always lived at sea, so I was worried we wouldn't fit in with $c.」

188:t_1:21.en:
$$メール$$
「It'll be fine, $$エイミー$$. We've got people from all kinds of worlds here.」

188:t_1:22.en:
$$ランド$$
「And in every world, people eat when they're hungry. I'm counting on another tasty meal today, $$エイミー$$.」

188:t_1:23.en:
$$エイミー$$
「Leave it to me, $$ランド$$.」

188:t_1:24.en:
$$エイミー$$
「Good luck to you too, $$レド$$ and $$チェインバー#pilot$$.」

188:t_1:25.en:
$$レド$$
「I'm busy preparing for atmospheric entry now. Let's talk later, $$エイミー$$.」

188:t_1:26.en:
$$エイミー$$
「Well... I can tell it's really difficult, but what is atmospheric entry?」

188:t_1:28.en:
$$チェインバー#pilot$$
「Descending to a planet with an atmosphere... It can be described as a struggle against frictional heat.」

188:t_1:30.en:
$n
「Put simply, it's heat produced by rubbing against the air.」

188:t_1:31.en:
$$レド$$
「You seem rather tired before the operation, $n.」

188:t_1:32.en:
$$シン$$
「That's because $$セツコ$$ put him through grueling solo atmospheric-entry simulations.」

188:t_1:33.en:
$$アルト$$
「Still, it's surprising... I never imagined $$セツコ$$ was such a strict coach.」

188:t_1:34.en:
$$セツコ$$
「If you give up over this level of training, you won't make it to the next step.」

188:t_1:38.en:
$$クルツ$$
「I thought you were the innocent type, but you've got it in you, $$セツコ$$.」

188:t_1:39.en:
$$マオ$$
「That Chief who trained you must have been quite a tough guy.」

188:t_1:41.en:
$$クルツ$$
「Too bad, $n. After private lessons with Miss $$スズネ$$, you didn't get sweet one-on-one coaching from $$セツコ$$.」

188:t_1:42.en:
$n
「I'm not you, $$クルツ$$. I wasn't thinking anything like that.」

188:t_1:43.en:
$n
「Though I didn't expect it to be this hard...」

188:t_1:44.en:
$$シン$$
「Don't think you'll always get all the perks.」

188:t_1:45.en:
$$かなめ$$
「$$シン$$... Keep talking like that, and I'll tell $$ルナマリア$$.」

188:t_1:47.en:
$$宗介$$
「You're showing signs of mental laxity.」

188:t_1:48.en:
$$マオ$$
「You're right. Want Sis $$マオ$$ to toughen you and $n up, Marine Corps style?」

188:t_1:49.en:
$$シン$$
「P-please give me a break, $$マオ$$!」

188:t_1:51.en:
$$エイミー$$
「Huh... Being a pilot really does come with all kinds of challenges.」

188:t_1:52.en:
$$レド$$
「$$チェインバー#pilot$$... I'd like to review the procedure once more too.」

188:t_1:53.en:
$$チェインバー#pilot$$
「Understood. Ensign $$レド$$, take your seat.」

188:t_1:54.en:
$$アルト$$
「Hey, $$レド$$. You don't need to do that.」

188:t_1:55.en:
$$宗介$$
「You're a soldier of the $$人類銀河同盟$$, which mainly fights in space. Why simulate atmospheric entry now?」

188:t_1:57.en:
$$チェインバー#pilot$$
「This unit possesses entry-sequence data but has never executed it either.」

188:t_1:59.en:
$$レド$$
「Yes... In fact, I'd never seen a habitable planet with an atmosphere with my own eyes.」

188:t_1:60.en:
$$チェインバー#pilot$$
「The same applies to this unit.」

188:t_1:61.en:
$$クルツ$$
「So that's how it is... We've fought aliens so many times, I thought planets like that were everywhere in the galaxy.」

188:t_1:62.en:
$$アルト$$
「Observations do suggest there are nearly ten billion Earth-like planets.」

188:t_1:64.en:
$$アルト$$
「But whether we can reach them is another matter.」

188:t_1:65.en:
$$アルト$$
「Space is vast. Emigrant fleets like our $$フロンティア$$ spend generations searching for habitable planets.」

188:t_1:67.en:
$$エイミー$$
「Beyond those stars are so many more stars, and the ocean of space goes on and on forever.」

188:t_1:68.en:
$$ランド$$
「And $$サイデリアル$$ came all the way to Earth, on the outskirts of the Milky Way, in that enormous universe.」

188:t_1:69.en:
$$クルツ$$
「That's a lot of trouble to go to, even if they want dimensional power.」

188:t_1:70.en:
$$シン$$
「I've wondered this for a while. What do the people who come to Earth for dimensional power intend to do with it?」

188:t_1:71.en:
$$セツコ$$
「...According to $$サルディアス$$, $$サイデリアル$$ plans to use dimensional power in the fighting at the galactic center.」

188:t_1:74.en:
$$レド$$
「It's true. Soldiers at the bottom like me get very little information, but...」

188:t_1:75.en:
$$レド$$
「Apparently $$サイデリアル$$, $$ヒディアーズ#keyword$$, and various other factions are clashing at the galactic center.」

188:t_1:76.en:
$$ランド$$
「Ten billion planets scattered across this huge universe, and they're still butting heads. They must have time to kill.」

188:t_1:77.en:
$$宗介$$
「But if they intend to use Earth's dimensional power in a galactic war, how will they transport it?」

188:t_1:80.en:
$$セツコ$$
「$$サルディアス$$ said that too. $$サイデリアル$$ is gathering $$スフィア$$s to transport dimensional power.」

188:t_1:81.en:
$$かなめ$$
「I see... So they use the $$スフィア$$s to control Earth's $$オリジン・ロー$$ directly.」

context_decisions: Pinion calls Astonaige Boss as workplace title, separate from Rand's missing mentor the Boss. Rand asks Amy to cook. Hibiki simulator training explains exhaustion. Ledo has no planetary entry experience despite space combat career.
uncertain: 188:t_1:28-30: source explains reentry as frictional heat; translated faithfully without correcting physics.
